trig.title: Trigonometry
trig.rightHint: Enter two values including at least one side. The right angle is at vertex C. a is opposite α, b is opposite β.
trig.needMore: Enter at least two values including one side (and valid values).
trig.obliqueHint: Enter three values including at least one side. Side a is opposite angle A, and so on.
trig.ambiguous: The data gives two possible triangles.
trig.needMoreOblique: Not enough data or the triangle does not exist. Enter three values including one side.

holes.title: Bolt holes and counterbores
holes.head: Head / part type
holes.noHeadSize: No dimensions for {{head}} in size {{size}}. Choose another size or "Custom dimensions".
holes.plateHint: Enter the plate thickness to get the remaining thickness under the counterbore and the minimum screw length.
holes.cskNote: Diameter = theoretical head diameter (ISO 7721) plus clearance. Measure the diameter at the surface.
holes.hexNote: Diameter is based on the head's across-corners size. A socket wrench needs a larger counterbore.
holes.lengthNote: Length measured under the head, including the washer. Thread run-out is not included in the engagement.
holes.lengthNoteCsk: Overall length of a countersunk screw (measured from the top of the head).

warn.noWasher: No washer in this size. Calculated without a washer.
warn.cskSmall: The countersink diameter is not larger than the hole diameter.
warn.cboreSmall: The counterbore diameter is not larger than the hole diameter.
warn.platePierced: The counterbore is deeper than the plate thickness.
warn.plateThin: Only a very thin layer of material remains under the counterbore.

holes.footer: Holes per ISO 273 (H12/H13/H14 tolerances), head dimensions per product standards. Counterbores include clearance, close to DIN 974-1. Check the standard if the drawing requires it.

un.title: Unified inch threads (UNC / UNF / UNEF)
un.depthExtNote: from max major diameter to root
un.minorNoMax: For class 3B and 8 TPI or coarser the standard gives the maximum only in its table.
un.footer: Dimensions per ASME B1.1, calculated with the standard's formulas and checked against Table 2 (e.g. 1/4-20 UNC, 1/2-13, 1-8, 1/4-28, 1/4-32). Check the standard's table if the drawing requires it.

acme.title: Acme threads (ASME B1.5)
acme.basicInfo: Pitch P = {{p}} · lead L = {{lead}} · lead angle {{angle}}°
acme.outOfRange: Outside the standard's range (1/4–5 in). Values are approximate.
acme.multiStart: Multi-start thread: tolerances are those of a single start; the standard recommends increasing them (Appendix B).
acme.rootFlatNote: tool tip width no larger than this value
acme.rootFlatNutNote: width of the groove bottom in the nut
acme.footer: General purpose 29° Acme thread, classes 2G/3G/4G per ASME B1.5, length of engagement up to 2D. Formulas from the standard; the 1/2-10 2G result matches its example. Check Table 10 of the standard if the drawing requires it.
acme.stubMajorNote: basic diameter, no tolerance in this calculator
acme.footerStub: Stub Acme 29°, thread height 0.3·P, class 2G per ASME B1.8, length of engagement up to 2D. Results match the standard's table (pitch and minor diameters, sizes 1/4–1 3/8 in); in two small sizes the minor diameter differs by 0.0001 in. Major diameter tolerances are not calculated. Check the standard if the drawing requires it.

rd.title: Round thread Rd (DIN 405)
rd.footer: Dimensions per DIN 405 tables (data from a gage manufacturer), pitch in threads per inch. Tolerances are fixed for each pitch. Check the standard if the drawing requires it.

bspt.title: Taper pipe thread R / Rc (ISO 7-1)
bspt.gaugeLength: Gauge plane distance from small end
bspt.taper: Taper 1:16 on diameter, half angle {{angle}}. Diameters grow by 0.0625 mm per 1 mm of length.
bspt.footer: Diameters at the gauge plane per ISO 7-1, others derived from the taper. Internal Rc has the same dimensions. Check lengths in the standard.

buttress.title: Buttress thread S (DIN 513)
buttress.basicInfo: 3°/30° form (33° total) · basic dimensions without tolerances
buttress.footer: Basic dimensions per DIN 513 (h3 = 0.86777·P, H1 = 0.75·P, R = 0.12427·P). Values may differ by 0.001 from the tables. Tolerance classes (7H…9c) from DIN 513 part 3 are not calculated, check the standard.

calc.title: Calculator
calc.hint: Tap a result above to insert it · hold to copy

pg.title: Steel conduit thread Pg (DIN 40430)
pg.footer: Basic dimensions per DIN 40430 (no tolerances). The Pg thread was withdrawn in 2000 and replaced by the 1.5 mm metric thread. Sizes Pg 29–48 show basic values with no metric equivalents listed.
